children.value: Check Your Understanding: Confidence Interval for the Mean Difference

children.label: Check Your Understanding: Confidence Interval for the Mean Difference

children.value: A publishing company wanted to test whether typing speed differs when using word processor A or word processor B. A random sample of 25 typists was selected, and the typing speeds (in words per minute) were recorded for each typist when using word processor A and then when using word processor B. (Which word processor was used first was determined for each typist by a coin flip.)
Based on the collected data, a 95% confidence interval for

children.html: μd\mu_dμd​

children.value: , the mean difference (word processor A − word processor B), was found to be (2.5, 7.8). The appropriate hypotheses for testing whether the typing speeds differ are the two-sided test

children.html: H0:μd=0H_0: \mu_d = 0H0​:μd​=0
Ha:μd≠0H_a: \mu_d \neq 0Ha​:μd​=0

model.question: Based on the confidence interval, what is the conclusion of the two-sided test at the 0.05 significance level?

choices.text: Reject H₀—typing speeds differ between the two word processors
choices.feedback: Correct! 0 falls outside the interval, so it is not a plausible value for μ_d, and we reject H₀—typing speeds differ between the two word processors.

choices.text: Do not reject H₀—0 is a plausible value for μ_d
choices.feedback: 0 is NOT inside (2.5, 7.8)—the interval starts at 2.5.

choices.text: The confidence interval cannot be used to carry out the test
choices.feedback: The interval method applies here directly, since the test is two-sided and the levels match (95% and 0.05).

model.question: What additional insight does the interval (2.5, 7.8) provide beyond the test conclusion?

choices.text: Typists average between 2.5 and 7.8 more words per minute with word processor A than with B
choices.feedback: Correct! Since the interval is entirely positive, typists are faster with word processor A—by between 2.5 and 7.8 words per minute, with 95% confidence.

choices.text: Typists are faster with word processor B
choices.feedback: The direction is the opposite: positive differences (A − B) mean A produced HIGHER speeds.

choices.text: Every typist types 2.5 to 7.8 words per minute faster with A
choices.feedback: The interval describes the mean difference, not the speeds of individual typists.

model.hint: The differences were computed as (A − B), and the whole interval is positive.
